classification.difficultyReason: Count unordered triangle pairs and use the supplied consecutive-vertices hint to identify three non-overlapping partitions, then subtract.

content.prompt: Ten points A, B, ..., J are arranged in order around a circle.

spec.description: Ten unlabelled point markers in circular order, without a connecting circumference. The uppermost marker retains its additional concentric outline. Decorative blue fill is replaced by ordinary black outlines.
spec.mathematics: Ten distinct points on a circle; no three are collinear.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many triangles can be drawn with these points as vertices?

answer.worked:
Choose any three of the ten points.
$$\begin{aligned}N&={}^{10}C_3\\&=120\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many pairs of such triangles can be drawn, if the vertices of the two triangles are distinct?

answer.worked:
Choose six distinct vertices in ${}^{10}C_6$ ways. From these, choose three for one triangle; the other three form the second triangle. Divide by $2$ because exchanging the two triangles gives the same pair: $\{A,B,C\},\{D,E,F\}$ and $\{D,E,F\},\{A,B,C\}$ are identical pairs.
$$\begin{aligned}N&={}^{10}C_6\times\frac{{}^{6}C_3}{2}\\&=210\times\frac{20}{2}\\&=2100\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: In how many such pairs will the triangles:

children.label: i
children.prompt:
not overlap?

Hint: For the triangles not to overlap, each triangle's vertices must be consecutive in the circular order of the six selected points. List the ways.

answer.worked:
For any six selected points, label them $A,B,C,D,E,F$ in circular order. There are three unordered partitions into consecutive triples:
$$\begin{gathered}\{A,B,C\},\{D,E,F\}\\\{B,C,D\},\{E,F,A\}\\\{C,D,E\},\{F,A,B\}.\end{gathered}$$
Thus
$$\begin{aligned}N&={}^{10}C_6\times3\\&=210\times3\\&=630.\end{aligned}$$

Overlapping and non-overlapping pairs are complementary.
$$\begin{aligned}N&=2100-630\\&=1470\end{aligned}$$
